title: Space Tourism
description: Turn a holiday into a space flight: name the craft and the place it leaves from (spaceship, shuttle, spaceport, space travel, trip and flight, suborbital and orbital) and the words the news report brought with it (billionaire, well-to-do, a face-off, a foothold, a deal, emerging, a couple of), read a definition by its first words (a place where…, a person who…, the act of…) and use it in both directions, to find a word and to judge a sentence, say an idiom or a proverb in your own words by keeping the idea and letting the image go (to see the world, to do the sights, The world is a book and those who do not travel read only a page), put the -ing form straight after the eighteen verbs that demand it (stop, enjoy, dislike, admit, consider, miss, finish, mind, imagine, deny, involve, postpone, delay, suggest, regret, avoid, practise, risk) and after a preposition, know the verbs that accept -ing and to + infinitive with no change of meaning (begin, continue, like, prefer, can't stand, cease), tell stopped working from stopped to eat, build opposites with the negative prefixes un-, in-, im-, il-, ir-, dis-, ab- and non- on adjectives, verbs and nouns, read the decimal point against the thousands comma, and hear the sound [ei] behind its five spellings
